context.pipeline_authenticity: unchanged: all analyze/draft outputs still carry the '[mock-llm]' echo prefix; no tweet.posted event exists yet; no LLM/social key in .env

opportunities.finding: Duplicate failure-diagnosis missions are now 71/137 = 52% of all missions in a 4h window (up from 26% of proposals in the 18:42 cycle) - the observer loop is the single largest consumer of mission budget and it re-diagnoses the same two missions (92395, 92756) every ~3 min

The Scout intel cycle itself ran 9 times in 4h (~54/day) and each run re-derived the same three findings (mock LLM, tweet.posted=0, duplicate diagnostics). Detection is saturated; the constraint is now execution/approval, not insight generation
Draft throughput (~8 tweets + 8 content drafts per 4h) has produced 0 posts - every growth hypothesis remains untestable in market, so all funnel metrics are currently synthetic

risks.risk: Insight volume (125/4h) is 100% mock-LLM echo, so growth dashboards will show linear 'growth' that contains zero information. If the cycle keeps emitting, a reader may mistake throughput for progress

Observer failure-diagnosis missions are self-perpetuating (each diagnosis creates a mission that can itself fail and trigger another diagnosis) - an unbounded feedback loop that crowds out real experiments
Publishing mock-echo text publicly would burn credibility, so the publish path must stay gated until a real LLM + social adapter is wired

nextExperiments.hypothesis: A novelty gate on the Scout intel cycle (hash of top finding + top risk + top experiment; skip proposal creation if the same hash exists in the last 24h) converts the hourly cycle from a noise generator into a change-detector
nextExperiments.metric: 'Scout intel cycle' missions/day <= 6 (from ~54) AND repeated identical finding-set hashes in 24h = 0

nextExperiments.hypothesis: Extending the existing (title, mission_id) dedupe to the two repeated failure-diagnosis missions reclaims ~50% of mission budget for growth work
One dry-run post_tweet step on an existing draft (still unimplemented since 18:42) creates the first publish-path baseline
nextExperiments.metric: tweet.posted count >= 1 within 24h with tweetId starting 'mock_'

decision: Run E1 first: the intel cycle currently spends ~54 missions/day re-stating known findings and is the cheapest thing to throttle while keeping scope to one gate + one hash table. Queue E2 (budget reclaim) and E3 (publish baseline) behind it. Do not enable live posting while LLM/social adapters are mocks.
diffFromPrevCycle: 18:42 cycle framed the gap as draft->publish throughput with the mock LLM as root cause. This cycle measures mission composition: duplicate failure-diagnosis missions now consume 52% of all missions (up from 26% of proposals), and the Scout cycle's own 9 runs/4h produced no state change - so the new lever is novelty gating + budget reclaim, not more analysis.
